source_snapshot.procedure: Use the tray leak self-test feature to simulate a leak.
source_snapshot.criteria: The tray detects the simulated leak, turns off, and sends the correct BMC signals.
source_snapshot.script: No bundle; 60/60 minutes; unique HW code/variant.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL; offers ipmitool sensor/SEL reads but no supported self-test trigger, complete response matrix, restoration or safe credential handling.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION/HIGH; retained Pending for exact vendor trigger, protective response, BMC events and recovery.

old_problem: No executable vendor interface is named and 'turn off' has no actuator/state meaning. Filtered IPMI reads cannot prove the self-test ran, the controller traversed the intended transient state, protective action occurred, or the tray returned safely to normal.
disposition_reason: Pending remains under ED-03/15/16/20 because a proprietary self-test command and authoritative protective-state oracle cannot be invented. The read-only IPMI/Redfish observation layer is draftable, but the HW tray/firmware owner must identify the supported trigger, exact valve/pump/rail behavior, event IDs/timing and reset path. This simulation stays distinct from row 2093's real PG25 leak and row 2095's GB-NV-PVP-owned variant.
decision_basis: XLSX row 2094, same-row DeepSeek, GPT V2, historical record, unique identity and ED-01 through ED-30 were reviewed; actual next formal row Functionality 2095 / Wistron-GB NV PVP HW-00018-V002 / 14ccca0d72d386fb was directly read from XLSX and manifest.
No standard IPMI command universally starts an OEM liquid-tray leak simulation; the trigger must be supplied for the exact controller/firmware.
Sensor/SEL listing is supporting evidence only and cannot replace proof of trigger acceptance or physical/controller protective transition.
'Turn off' needs an exact HW-owned map to sensor, valve, pump, tray rail and/or system states plus maximum latency and permitted service impact.
Capture unfiltered, timestamped pre/during/post controller, sensor, Redfish and SEL evidence; grep-only results may hide contradictory or recovery events.
Credentials must use an approved secret mechanism and authenticated channel; inline `-P` secrets, host bypass and log clearing are rejected.
The self-test is invoked once; stop on any real-leak indication, unexpected actuator/power change, BMC instability or restore failure and never substitute physical coolant.
No vendor trigger, IPMI/Redfish query, simulated or physical leak, actuator/power action, restoration, retry or DUT operation was performed.

test_case.test_name: HW tray vendor leak self-test with full state correlation — TRIGGER PENDING
test_case.purpose: Using the exact supported HW tray self-test, prove a simulated leak causes the specified detection and protective state, emits the correct BMC events, and returns to the defined normal no-leak state without applying coolant.
required_package: HW tray/controller owner-approved self-test command/interface and compatible firmware
Versioned tray/sensor/valve/pump/rail/system-state response and timing matrix
Expected IPMI/Redfish/SEL identifiers, severities, assertion/deassertion and persistence
Secret-safe authenticated BMC access and complete unfiltered telemetry capture
Approved service-impact boundary, abort conditions, reset/restoration and recovery
test_case.test_command: DO NOT INVENT OR RUN A GENERIC SELF-TEST. Once the exact HW vendor trigger and oracle are approved, securely capture full tray/controller/sensor/actuator and BMC log baselines; after point authorization invoke the supported simulation once, retain complete trigger status and timestamp every expected transient response/event; then use the documented reset/restoration and prove the exact normal final state. Read-only `ipmitool`/Redfish collection may support evidence but must be unfiltered and must not expose credentials. Never introduce coolant or retry after anomaly.
test_case.expected_result: Cannot be finalized until the vendor trigger and response matrix are signed. The approved simulation must assert the mapped leak state, perform the exact specified protective turn-off within limits, emit the required BMC signals, avoid a real-leak condition/unapproved service effect and restore every mapped state to normal.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: No PASS while trigger, turn-off meaning, event/timing matrix and restored-state oracle are unknown. After unlock, PASS requires one accepted supported trigger, complete causal transient evidence, all exact protective/BMC responses and verified restoration. FAIL on unsupported trigger, missing/late/wrong response, real leak, unexpected outage, contradictory log or restoration failure.
safety_gate: Gate CLOSED until controller/firmware compatibility, exact trigger, service impact and recovery are approved.
Require human point approval before the single self-test invocation.
Confirm the path is simulation-only and preserve complete unfiltered evidence; no physical fluid or interlock bypass.
Stop without retry on real-leak indication, unexpected actuator/power effect, BMC instability or failed return to normal.
expected_evidence: Exact HW row/variant/hash, controller/firmware identity and approved trigger
Signed sensor/actuator/power/BMC response and timing matrix plus approvals
Complete timestamped pre-state and full trigger request/response/status
During-test raw controller/sensor/valve/pump/rail telemetry and physical operator observation where required
Documented restoration, exact normal final state, post-health, no-coolant/no-retry audit and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: If the trigger is rejected, behavior differs, a real leak appears or restoration fails, stop and preserve all state/logs. Do not retry, use coolant or guess a reset. Apply only the documented vendor recovery and leave affected pumps/valves/rails or node isolated until owner release.
